 THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO QUASH THE ENDORSEMENT ISSUED BY THE RESPONDENT NO.3 VIDE ANNEXURE-D DATED 13.04.2016 AND TO DIRECT THE RESPONDENT NO.3 TO HEREIN DISPOSE OF THE APPEAL ON MERITS FILED BY THE PETITIONERS VIDE ANNX-B IN CASE APPEAL NO.CR18/2015-16 AND TO GRANT SUCH OTHER RELIEFS.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B' GROUP, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE E.S.INDIRESH  -3-  NC: 2024:KHC:50629  WP No. 33363 of 2018  ORAL ORDER
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties 2.

In this writ petition, the petitioners are assailing the Endorsement dated 13.04.2016 (Annexure-D) inter-aila sought for direction to respondent No.3 to dispose of the appeal on merits produced at Annexure-B to the writ petition.
Sri K Srinivasa vs The Spl Land Acquisition Officer on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71113429/
2 3. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties, it is not in dispute that, the land belonging to the petitioners was acquired by the respondent-authorities for the improvement /construction of National Highway-4 (Mulbagil-Kolar Bangalore Section) and accordingly, award notice issued on 16.07.2008 (Annexure-A).

The petitioners being not satisfied with the compensation awarded by the respondent-authorities, have filed appeal in Appeal NC:
2024:KHC:50629 No.CR18/2015-16 as per Annexure-B and the respondent No.3 by Endorsement dated 13.04.2016 rejected the appeal on the ground of delay and laches.

4. In the backdrop of the arguments advanced by the learned counsel appearing for the parties and on careful examination of the provisions contained under Section 3G(5) of the National Highway Authority Act, 1956, the aggrieved party has to approach the competent authority at the earliest.

Taking into consideration the fact that, though the petitioners have received the compensation from the Special Land Acquisition Officer on 12.02.2009, however, have not approached the Arbitrator,
seeking enhancement of the compensation at the earliest.

Therefore, in view of the declaration of law made by this Court in W.A.No.31066 of 2012 and W.ANo.31094-96 of 2012 in the case of Y.Yunis vs. National Highways Authority of India and others disposed of on NC: 2024:KHC:50629 12.10.2012, the aggrieved party has to approach the Arbitrator appointed by the Central Government within reasonable period and taking into consideration the fact that, the petitioners have filed the appeal on 02.12.2015, nearly after lapse of a period of six years from the receipt of the compensation awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, there is no infirmity in the Endorsement dated 13.04.2016 issued by the respondent-authorities.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I do not find merit in the writ petition.
In the result, the writ petition is dismissed.
